examples.japanese: {岩|いわ}が{突出|とっしゅつ}している。
{建物|たてもの}の{一部|いちぶ}が{道路|どうろ}に{突出|とっしゅつ}している。
examples.english: Part of the building protrudes into the road.

examples.japanese: {海面|かいめん}から{突出|とっしゅつ}した{岩礁|がんしょう}に{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Caution is needed for the reefs jutting out from the sea surface.

examples.japanese: あの{選手|せんしゅ}の{成績|せいせき}は{突出|とっしゅつ}している。
examples.english: That player's results are exceptionally outstanding.

examples.japanese: {突出|とっしゅつ}した{才能|さいのう}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}だ。
examples.english: They are someone with outstanding talent.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{高齢化率|こうれいかりつ}が{世界|せかい}で{突出|とっしゅつ}して{高|たか}い。
examples.english: Japan has an exceptionally high aging rate compared to the rest of the world.

notes:
Used both literally for physical protrusion and figuratively for something or someone that stands out conspicuously. The figurative sense is very common in news, sports, and business contexts to describe exceptional performance or prominent figures.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {突出|とっしゅつ}した{才能|さいのう}: outstanding talent
- {突出|とっしゅつ}した{成績|せいせき}: exceptional results
- {突出|とっしゅつ}して{高|たか}い: conspicuously high
- {突出|とっしゅつ}{部分|ぶぶん}: protruding part

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {傑出|けっしゅつ}: outstanding, distinguished — used exclusively for people and their abilities
- {卓越|たくえつ}: excellence — emphasizes surpassing quality, more formal
- {目立|めだ}つ: to stand out — everyday word, less formal than {突出|とっしゅつ}
